clue.text: A US lawyer writing as US president

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American public prosecutor
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a piece of writing

explanation.surface: An American attorney who writes under the guise of a president.
explanation.definitionFit: John Adams and John Quincy Adams were the second and sixth holders of the White House office.

clue.text: "Beware the pine-tree's withered branch! Beware the awful _____" (Longfellow)

definitions.text: "Beware the pine-tree's withered branch! Beware the awful _____" (Longfellow)

parts.words: "Beware the pine-tree's withered branch! Beware the awful _____" (Longfellow)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank from Longfellow's poem Excelsior, where an old man warns the climbing youth of mountain dangers

explanation.surface: A line of Victorian verse warning of mountain perils.
explanation.walkthrough: The missing word comes from the old man's warning in Longfellow's poem Excelsior, about a mass of snow sliding down the mountainside.
explanation.definitionFit: The blank is a sudden fall of snow and ice down a slope, a peril for alpine travellers.

clue.text: Bill and Edward played together

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
Ted is a familiar form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Two men named Bill and Edward performed side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name beside Edward, but it means an account, abbreviated AC.
explanation.definitionFit: To perform a role on stage is to have played a part.

clue.text: Vociferousness of the awkward resident about a hundred

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the numeral
awkward signals the letters of resident are placed in an ungainly new order

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: The noise made by a difficult local person aged about a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges RESIDENT, and 'about' puts that jumble around C.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrillness or harsh loudness is the quality of being noisily insistent.

clue.text: Source of income for a top man

explanation.surface: Looking for a money-earner to support the boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A capital sum earning interest is called the principal; the head of a school or firm is also the principal.

clue.text: Cook is a petty criminal

explanation.surface: The chef is a small-time crook.
explanation.definitionFit: One who cooks eggs gently in water is one sense; one who takes game illegally is the other.

clue.text: One about to settle in the country

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
RE means about or concerning
to land is to come to rest, to settle

explanation.surface: A person intending to emigrate and put down roots abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Eire is the nation occupying most of the island west of Great Britain.

clue.text: Order form

explanation.surface: A request slip for buying goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank in biological taxonomy or a social grade is one sense; a school year group, called a form in Britain, is the other.

clue.text: Strain through business being dead?

parts.note: per means through or by means of
CO is short for company, a business
the late someone is a person who has died

explanation.surface: Is a company's failure a struggle?
explanation.walkthrough: Strain looks like effort, but it means filter, as coffee does.
explanation.definitionFit: To filter a liquid slowly through a mass, as coffee does through grounds, is to drip through it.

clue.text: Cut the man!

explanation.surface: An order to wound a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce a boil with a surgical blade is one sense; a male first name is the other.

clue.text: Post protection

parts.note: read Post as 'after' rather than mail: looking after someone once treatment is over

explanation.surface: Security for the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Care given to a patient following an operation or hospital stay is the follow-up support named here.

clue.text: Scottish island administered by retired academician

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the abbreviation for academician is written backwards

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
to run a business is to administer it, so administered gives ran

explanation.surface: An island in Scotland governed by an elderly academic who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' turns RA (Royal Academician) into AR, which goes before RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Arran is an island in the Firth of Clyde off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Some said education should be subsidised

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A claim that schooling deserves state money.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'should be subsidised' as the definition, but the answer is a past participle meaning 'subsidised' alone; 'should be' is a link and keeps the swap grammatical.
explanation.definitionFit: A school or project that receives public money is aided, that is, financially supported.

clue.text: 4 ac's sound though grave testimonial

parts.note: 4 across is a principal, the head of a school, so the principal's is head's
a tone is a musical sound

explanation.surface: The headmaster's voice sounds solemn though he is writing a reference.
explanation.walkthrough: '4 ac's' points to the answer of 4 across, read here as a head teacher, with the possessive kept as S.
explanation.definitionFit: A gravestone is a memorial stone, a tribute set over a burial plot.

clue.text: People who are late occupy his attention

definitions.text: People who are late occupy his attention

parts.words: People who are late occupy his attention
parts.note: late here means dead, not tardy: the official whose job is investigating deaths

explanation.surface: Someone constantly bothered by unpunctual folk.
explanation.definitionFit: This official holds inquests into sudden or unexplained deaths.

clue.text: Cracks discerned, so set aside

indicators.note: cracks means breaks up, so the letters of the next word are broken and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Fissures were spotted, so the plan was shelved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracks' looks like a noun, but it is the verb that breaks up DISCERNED.
explanation.definitionFit: A law or order that is revoked or annulled has been cancelled officially.

clue.text: If the editor backed a worker it could appear daring

indicators.note: backed means set in reverse, so the run of if plus the editor is read backwards

parts.note: ED is the standard abbreviation for editor
a worker ant is the classic crossword worker

explanation.surface: Supporting an employee may look like a bold move by a newspaper boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns IF + ED into DEFI, which goes in front of ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone daring or bold in the face of authority is openly resistant to it.

clue.text: Not to be made light of

definitions.text: Not to be made light of

parts.words: Not to be made light of
parts.note: light here is the flame sense: something that cannot be set alight, not something that must be taken seriously

explanation.surface: A warning to take something seriously.
explanation.definitionFit: Material that resists catching fire is flame-resistant.

clue.text: A Continental summit meeting?

parts.note: the French phrase literally means head to head, so a summit (head) meeting in a European tongue

explanation.surface: A conference of European leaders.
explanation.definitionFit: A private conversation between two people, from the French for head to head.

clue.text: Oriental form of 19

indicators.note: form of says the letters of that answer are reshaped into another word

parts.note: 19 down's answer, the closest or most stingy

explanation.surface: A version from the East of another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' rearranges NEAREST, the answer to 19 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Something from Asia or the Orient is described as belonging to the East.

clue.text: The most penny-pinching 18 organisation

indicators.note: organisation means arranging, so the letters of that answer are put in a new order

parts.note: 18 across's answer, meaning oriental

explanation.surface: The stingiest group from another entry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' rearranges EASTERN, the answer to 18 across. Near is an old word for mean with money.
explanation.definitionFit: Near can mean stingy or tight-fisted, so the superlative is the meanest.

clue.text: Crawler dispatched without hesitation by party leader

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the word for dispatched wraps the other pieces

parts.note: something dispatched has been sent
ER is the sound of a speaker hesitating

indicators.note: the leader of party is its first letter

explanation.surface: A grovelling hanger-on promptly sent off by the head of a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking, so SENT goes round ER and P (the first letter of 'party').
explanation.definitionFit: A snake moves along the ground on its belly, so it is a creature that creeps.

clue.text: Rail over this spy planted in advance

explanation.surface: A railway beam and a secret agent placed long before.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden beam under railway track carries the rails; an agent embedded for years before activation is the other sense.

clue.text: Bring back control — the country's behind it

indicators.note: behind it says the word for country follows the word for control

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as in keeping a tight rein
a state is a country; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Restoring authority, with the nation backing the move.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone to a former post is to return them to it.

clue.text: Revolting person getting a step up

explanation.surface: A rebel getting promoted.
explanation.definitionFit: One who rises in revolt is one sense; the vertical part of a stair is the other.

clue.text: The setting for a confrontation

explanation.surface: Where a showdown takes place.
explanation.definitionFit: The place where events happen is one sense; a noisy row, as in 'make a fuss', is the other.

clue.text: Like getting in quiet word of thanks for the food

indicators.note: getting in says the word for like goes inside the other pieces

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning quiet
TA is British informal for thank you
as means like, as in 'white as snow'

explanation.surface: Muttering a soft thank-you for one's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting in' places AS between P and TA. TA is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Spaghetti, penne and the like are Italian staples made from durum wheat dough.

clue.text: The turf points a way

parts.note: S and W are compass points, south and west
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: The grass shows the direction to take.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of grassy ground or lawn is a sod-covered expanse.

clue.text: Left inside edge

indicators.note: inside says the abbreviation for left is placed within the word for edge

parts.note: the side of something is its edge

explanation.surface: A shot in cricket or tennis that clips the inner rim on the left.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: L placed inside SIDE (edge) gives a word meaning to edge, that is, move crabwise.
explanation.definitionFit: To move furtively or sideways is to slip along cautiously, as when one inches along a wall.

clue.text: One page is being rewritten in this secret work

indicators.note: a page rewritten has its contents reworked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Redrafting a sheet of a classified document.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being rewritten' rearranges the letters of ONE PAGE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is covert intelligence-gathering, the business of agents.

clue.text: Memorable revolutionary character

parts.note: a red is a communist revolutionary
a letter of the alphabet is a character

explanation.surface: An unforgettable rebel figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A red-letter day is a special one, from saints' days printed in red in church calendars.
explanation.definitionFit: A notable day worth remembering is called a red-letter day.

clue.text: Sweet nonsense

explanation.surface: Sugary drivel.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft milky confection is one sense; evasive waffle or a dodge is the other.
